tools.name: Google AI Studio (Gemini API)
tools.what_you_get: Free tier, no card: roughly 15 requests/min and ~1,000-1,500/day on Flash models.
tools.caveat: Pro models left the free tier in April 2026, and model ids get retired with little notice — pin an exact one.

tools.name: Groq
tools.what_you_get: Free tier with very high daily request counts on smaller Llama models, and the fastest inference of anything free.
tools.caveat: Per-minute token limits bite before the daily request limit does.

tools.name: xAI (Grok) API
tools.what_you_get: $25 of credit on sign-up. That is all.
tools.caveat: NOT a free tier. The $150/month data-sharing programme ended in May 2025, but plenty of blog posts still recommend it.

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.what_you_get: One API key for many models, including a rotating set marked `:free`.
tools.caveat: Which models are free changes often, and free ones are rate-limited and can queue.

tools.name: Hugging Face
tools.what_you_get: Free hosted inference for many open models, plus free Spaces to host a demo (Docker supported).
tools.caveat: Free Spaces sleep when idle, so a judge clicking your link may wait for a cold start.

tools.name: Supabase
tools.what_you_get: Free: Postgres (500 MB), authentication with 50,000 monthly active users, 1 GB file storage, 500k edge-function calls, 2 projects.
tools.caveat: Free projects pause after about a week of inactivity — wake it before you demo.

tools.name: Clerk
tools.what_you_get: Drop-in sign-in UI with a free tier for small monthly active user counts.
tools.caveat: Check the current MAU allowance; it is the limit that matters and it moves.

tools.name: Neon
tools.what_you_get: Free serverless Postgres, ~0.5 GB, with no pause on inactivity.
tools.caveat: Compute suspends when idle, so the first query after a quiet spell is slow.

tools.name: Upstash
tools.what_you_get: Free Redis and Kafka on a per-request basis — good for rate limiting and queues.

tools.name: Cloudflare Pages
tools.what_you_get: Free static hosting: unlimited bandwidth and sites, 500 builds a month.

tools.name: Vercel
tools.what_you_get: Free hobby tier for frontends and serverless functions, deploying straight from a repo.
tools.caveat: Hobby is non-commercial, and function execution limits are tight.

tools.name: GitHub Pages
tools.what_you_get: Free static hosting for public repos, with unlimited Actions minutes to build it.
tools.caveat: Static only — no server-side code. This site runs on it.

tools.name: Slidev
tools.what_you_get: Open source. Write slides in Markdown, get animations, code highlighting and live components.
tools.caveat: Built for developers — it expects you to be comfortable in a terminal.

tools.name: Marp
tools.what_you_get: Open source. Markdown to slides, with a VS Code extension and PDF export.

tools.name: reveal.js
tools.what_you_get: Open source HTML presentation framework — the classic, and still the most flexible.

tools.name: Excalidraw
tools.what_you_get: Free hand-drawn-style diagrams. The fastest way to draw an architecture slide judges can follow.

tools.name: asciinema
tools.what_you_get: Free terminal recording that stays selectable text, not a blurry video.

tools.name: shadcn/ui
tools.what_you_get: Open source. Copy-paste React components you own outright, built on Radix and Tailwind.

tools.name: Aceternity UI
tools.what_you_get: Free animated React/Tailwind components — the kind of motion that makes a demo look expensive.
tools.caveat: Heavy effects can tank performance on the laptop you demo from.

tools.name: Lucide
tools.what_you_get: Open source icon set, 1,000+ icons, tree-shakeable.

tools.name: react-three-fiber
tools.what_you_get: Open source React renderer for three.js — 3D and shader effects in the browser.
tools.caveat: About 245 KB gzipped with three.js. Load it lazily or your first paint suffers.

tools.name: data.gov.in
tools.what_you_get: India's open government data — census, transport, agriculture, health.
tools.caveat: Quality varies a lot by dataset, and some downloads are stale.

tools.name: Hugging Face Datasets
tools.what_you_get: Hundreds of thousands of open datasets, loadable in one line of Python.

tools.name: Kaggle
tools.what_you_get: Large dataset library plus free GPU/TPU notebook hours each week.

tools.name: Cloudflare Tunnel
tools.what_you_get: Free public HTTPS URL for something running on your laptop — for demoing a webhook or a phone.

tools.name: Hoppscotch
tools.what_you_get: Open source API client in the browser. No account needed, no 400 MB download.

tools.name: Resend
tools.what_you_get: Free transactional email tier — enough to demo sign-up or notification flows.
tools.caveat: Sending to arbitrary addresses needs a verified domain; test mode is limited to your own.
